# A rewrite that does not type-check is discarded: the package is compiled from
# its original source, the build succeeds, and the log says why. Here the
# parameter named simd shadows the package the rewrite imports.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=example.com/app/vec
exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
! stdout .
! stderr .
cmpenv log log.want

exec ./app
cmp stdout want.out

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- vec/vec.go --
package vec

// The parameter named simd shadows the package the rewrite would import.
func AddInt32s(simd int, dst, a, b []int32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i] + int32(simd)
	}
}

func Add(simd int, dst, a, b []int32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/vec"
)

func main() {
	d := make([]int32, 3)
	vec.Add(0, d, []int32{1, 2, 3}, []int32{10, 20, 30})
	fmt.Println(d)
}
-- want.out --
[11 22 33]
-- log.want --
kept example.com/app/vec: rewritten source rejected: $WORK/vec/vec.go:14:19: simd.LoadInt32sPart undefined (type int has no field or method LoadInt32sPart)
